clues: This city lies in Rajasthan, in western India. It stands on the Berach River, a stream that flows into the Banas.
Almost all the rain here falls in the summer monsoon months. Outside those wet months, the land gets very little rain at all.
In 1303, the ruler Alauddin Khalji sacked this city for the first time. That attack opened a long tale of sieges here.
Foes sacked this city three times in all. The last sack was in 1568, by the Mughal ruler Akbar.
The city's fort is one of the largest forts in India and in Asia. Few forts anywhere on the continent can match its size.
